utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I notice that Mr. Simic, Mr. Milan Simic, is not in Court, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, my client is very sick, I should say, and he -- he wasn't able to come today. He waived his right, though, to be present today at the Court as well, as yesterday. And I don't really know at this moment, I cannot inform the Trial Chamber how long will it take, because he's under -- he's taking some medicaments. So I really don't know. It might happen that he comes tomorrow, but this is under question mark still. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. We can proceed, and we will inform the Trial Chamber accordingly for tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes. I see Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: You see both of us, if Your Honour pleases, perhaps if I may go first. If I could just assist the Chamber with a few matters that arose out of yesterday's proceedings. First of all Mr. Pantelic's inquiry regarding statements made by this witness. We checked our records, and the Prosecution can confirm that every statement and every set of notes that it has in its possession have been disclosed and provided to the Defence. Indeed, in the course of cross-examination, every statement and every set of notes has been in fact referred to in the evidence, bar one statement, which is a statement taken on the 27th of July, 1994, which was taken at the MUP in Bosnia, and that hasn't been raised in evidence thus far. But it was certainly provided to the Defence, and there are receipts. We have receipts dated the 15th of May of this year indicating that that particular statement was provided as well. So the upshot is everything's been provided. Just on that issue, however, I would ask Defence counsel to think carefully before making those sorts of requests in court. I understand their position, but nonetheless, seeking -- getting that sort of information about what's been provided is no easy matter, and it really takes the case manager away from a lot of other important tasks that the Prosecution would like him to be attending to in the evenings. I would ask the Defence counsel to think carefully before they make those requests. This statement was -- as I said, all material was provided and it's all been referred to in cross-examination except that one statement and that was provided back then. As I said, I repeat my request to Defence counsel to consider that issue carefully. It's not a question of simply going and looking up one document, it does involve quite a bit of work to go over material that's already been provided to them. So that's all I wanted to say about the issue raised by Mr. Pantelic. I believe on -- another matter is the statement of this witness that the Defence say was taken in the SUP office in Bosanski Samac. That statement was provided to the Prosecution, as I said, yesterday, by Mr. Lukic, and he will confirm that, I'm sure, shortly. And finally, if Your Honours please, on one matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This document you're talking about, this is D -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry I should have mentioned that. D22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: /3 MR. DI FAZIO: /3 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Serbo-Croat. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is the one actually. You're saying that was provided by the Defence to the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. And Mr. Lukic can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: And finally, there is just a matter that I detected earlier, and that's this: In D24/3, which is the judgement of the Bijeljina court, the translation of the judgement of the Bijeljina court, it says -- it's dated, if you look at that particular document in the top left-hand corner, 21st of August, 1993. That must be a mistake. I've shown it to Mr. Lukic, and if you look at the B/C/S version, D24/3 ter ID, it's the 21st of June, 1993. Just the dates. You see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: So the August date -- and given the minor controversies over dates and times as far as this statement is concerned, that could be important, so we should have an accurate translation. Can I draw that to the Chamber's attention, and could we, I don't know, perhaps by court order alter the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me find out from Mr. Lukic. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What date does the Defence maintain?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. The Prosecutor showed me this inconsistency between the English translation and the original document, and what I found out from the statement during the cross-examination of the witness was that the trial took place in June. Perhaps he can confirm that now. So I think that in that sense, the B/C/S document is beyond dispute and I think it's a mistake in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe I can ask the witness as to when the trial took place. Was it June 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: If I could also add one thing. In the English translation, if you look into the first paragraph, line 6, it actually does state 21st of June, 1993, that the court was sitting and rendering the judgement. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I think that confirms it beyond all doubt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: So that August should go -- sorry, 21st of August should go and 6th of -- 21st of June substituted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we all agree that Exhibit 24/3, it should be June and not August. MR. DI FAZIO: So perhaps it could be altered. I don't know how you'd normally proceed. A simple handwriting alteration should be enough if it's done by the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The record is there. It should go back, of course, to the translation people as well for the exhibit itself to be corrected. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, you are through? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Before -- Mr. Pantelic, just wait. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to talk about two things. Before the Prosecution says what their stand is, I would like to now provide to the registry and the Trial Chamber the documents of documents 26/3 ter ID and document 23/3 ter. I didn't have copies of that document yesterday, so one is for the registry and the rest is for the Trial Chamber. In response to what my learned friend the Prosecutor has said, I would like to I apologise to the Chamber and to the Prosecution regarding my statement of yesterday, because I really did think that I had received this document from the Prosecution. Shortly before the questioning -- the examination of this witness last December, we exchanged documents here in the courtroom, so I received a judgement from the Prosecution, and I did have a statement. In any case, the Prosecution received this document from me, and this is document D22 ter ID, the statement of the witness provided to the SUP. The original of this document is not in my possession. I've checked my documents here and also all the documents that I have. I checked them through my investigator in my office in Belgrade. I completely agree with the view of the Trial Chamber for a -- that there must be an original in order to carry out a handwriting expertise. I spoke with my learned friend the Prosecutor this morning regarding this problem, and I propose the following, but I would just like to ask the Trial Chamber to allow me to state what the procedure is according to the regulations which was in force then in the territory of the former Yugoslavia and also before the military tribunal in Bijeljina at the time of the proceedings. The essence is as follows: A statement which is taken in a police station is taken in three copies. One copy remains in the records of the police station. Two copies are provided to the public Prosecutor. The public Prosecutor, if he decides to initiate legal proceedings, will provide the case files and all the evidence to the investigative judge along with that statement. So one copy will be left in the possession of the public Prosecutor, and the second copy will be given to the investigative judge. The Trial Chamber before which the case appears of a certain person does not have the right to look at the statement given before the SUP, and it's not evidence before a Trial Chamber, except in strictly determined conditions in case it's subject to the strictest fine, and if the person that is being tried agrees with that. So it means that the statement which is provided to the court remains under seal with the investigative judge, which means that the original of the statement, the original statement could be kept in one of those three places. Through my investigator, I obtained copies of that statement, and I provided them to the Chamber. So I'm afraid that I may not be able to get from the authorities of Republika Srpska the originals. So my suggestion to the Prosecution was to provide in a reasonable date, and I will try to do my best to provide one of those originals. If I do not obtain such an original, then I will not move for handwriting expertise. But I think it would be interesting for this legal proceedings to ask for the case files regarding not only about this witness but other witnesses who were also before -- appeared before the court in Bijeljina in view of the accused's rights to a fair trial. I think it would be something that would be in important for this Trial Chamber, and I will try, to the best of my ability, to obtain these documents. So I would like to be given a certain period of time within which I can try to obtain this document. There's no need for the witness to give his signature on a separate piece of paper. The Prosecution already has in their statement -- in his statement to them his signature. So if necessary, then we will act on the basis of that in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to be sure that from what you have submitted, it means that the court in Bijeljina which tried the witness, the ones who delivered the judgement D24/3, do have one of the original copies of D22.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. According to the laws in force at that time, all the case materials, including the evidence -- including the statement, which is D22 ter ID, are kept at the court in Bijeljina with the investigative judge in his documents or in the case file itself under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, you can do what you can to see if you can obtain those documents. If you have any problems, you should apply by motion so that the Trial Chamber can issue the relevant orders to the relevant authorities, according to our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and then maybe we can have an original copy. Because the Trial Chamber would like to make sure that whatever examination the handwriting expert deals with is properly conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: The other thing perhaps I might remind you is, and ask you is whether each of the copies is signed separately or is there some sort of a carbon paper on which he signs on the original and then the signature appears on the other copies. Because then when you do provide a copy to this court, the signature has to be clear, very clear, and I think you should ascertain that before you bring the copy in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to my information, Your Honour Judge Singh, each copy is signed individually, and all of those -- each of those three copies represents an original. And I thank the Court for its decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And in addition to what Judge Singh has asked, when you look at D22, it's typed. Yeah. I was wondering whether that is how the statements are actually taken, typed or in longhand and then typed later. What are your instructions on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no rule about that. Sometimes, according to my information, even though I've never worked at the SUP myself but I did have access to such evidence, sometimes the person is asked to write out the whole statement, in which case the whole statement is handwritten. Sometimes he's asked to speak, to talk, and then the authorised official types up the statement at the same time as he's speaking and then the person being questioned signs statement. But according to the regulations in force at that time in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this was also the law which was applied in the territory of Republika Srpska, the person is just asked to provide a statement. But this is also in accordance with the Penal Code which was in force in the entire territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If my memory serves me right, I think the witness kept saying that the officer who was asking him questions already had a piece of paper onto which things were written. So I'll clear this with the witness so that we're sure at the time that he was being questioned what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to ask this of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We want to know whether anybody was recording and how they were recording, in longhand, typing, all the details at the time he was being interrogated, regarding D22. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume you've heard what the Trial Chamber is in interested in, and I am interested in that as well. I would like to ask you a few questions about the procedure itself when you were giving a statement to Mr. Savic. First all, was anybody else there present except for Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a duty police officer who was standing behind me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While Mr. Savic was taking your statement, was he typing anything out on a typewriter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Savic have any piece of paper in his hand which he showed you and which he asked you to sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did have a piece of paper which contained a list of 10 or 11 persons, among which was also my name, and it was a list of the scouts unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained to us that this was a paper which he was waving at you. It was proof which he showed to you in regard to your membership of the scouts unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a piece of paper in his hand which he asked you to sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a typist in that room to whom he was dictating something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think the matter has been sufficiently clarified now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just one more question to the witness. As you were answering the questions put to you, was the official writing down your answers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any point, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: No, thank you. Your Honour asked the question that I was going to ask -- I suggest should be asked, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just one or two more questions. How long were you with this Officer Savic that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 20 minutes to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: And you left the room then. Did you come back to sign anything later that day or the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We can go back to Mr. Lazarevic. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more clarification regarding the question by Judge Singh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps receive any kind of piece of paper from the SUP over the next several days to sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, we can continue with your cross-examination. Mr. Pantelic, you wanted to respond to Mr. Di Fazio's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Actually, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- with your permission about this issue about the statement from 1994 which might be of importance for ongoing proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honours. I made a short inquiry among my colleagues, and it seems to us that we didn't receive this statement from Orasje MUP from 1994, and I would be very grateful to our learned colleagues if they can just show us this copy so that we can know what is actually going on. And the other thing, Your Honours, it is our understanding that the Office of Prosecution is not in possession of any other statements from the witnesses in this cases from sources of Bosnian police or Bosnian intelligence service and that actually, in this particular case, they are finished with the discovery process to the Defence. I would like confirmation from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You may sit down then. Are you through? Yes. I would just ask you, Mr. Di Fazio, on the Orasje MUP 1994 statement. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I've got a copy here. It's got some handwriting on it, but I'm happy to provide it once again to the Defence, if that will assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And as far as discovery is concerned, well, I -- I'll repeat what I said earlier. We've handed over everything that we've got emanating from this witness in terms of statements and notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So when are you going to provide that? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Soon? MR. DI FAZIO: Now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to say that under Rule 68, of course the Defence are entitled to receive any documents that the Prosecution may have or may indeed come across even during the proceedings, even after the proceedings. The reason for this is that they're entitled to any document that may be of assistance to them, to the accused persons. And also the Trial Chamber is entitled to any documents that might have probative value. So that is important. So when they are asking for any sources from anywhere, they are simply obliging their clients under their duties to be diligent, as some of the Appeals Chamber decisions have indicated. They always have -- if they are put on inquiry, it is their duty to find out and make sure that if there are any documents, they have access to them. MR. DI FAZIO: The Prosecution is alive to that issue and that concern of the Trial Chamber and all the Trial Chambers in this Tribunal. I might also add that statements are one of the easiest things to identify and hand over in terms of Rule 68, so I just don't see that there could be any problem as far as disclosure is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't want to take any more -- any time here. After brief consultation, my colleagues confirm that they didn't receive this Orasje statement during the discovery process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During the break we shall contact our colleagues of Prosecution and we shall and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Resolve the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'm just wondering. Mr. Pantelic, in his -- not that statement but the previous intervention had asked the Prosecution concerning the discovery process being over with respect to witnesses, in the plural, in this case, and I believe I heard you, Mr. Di Fazio, to respond by saying that yes indeed all documents with respect to this particular witness in front of us had been disclosed. So I'm a little bit at odds with what Mr. Pantelic said and what you responded. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I was -- I was confining my remarks to this particular witness regarding disclosure because that's the context in which it arose. Is Your Honour now asking me about the issue disclosure generally in the case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Rather it's not myself asking; it's what Mr. Pantelic asked you. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, you're quite right when you say the issue is -- and -- an ongoing thing, and indeed there is an exercise in disclosure being conducted at the moment in conjunction with the Defence regarding a collection of documents. That is being conducted by my colleague Ms. Reidy, and I can't say that I have first-hand knowledge of just how that is progressing, but I can say that it is progressing and I can say that the Prosecution is alive to it and concerned about it, and I can say that the Defence are participating in that. So whether it is all disclosure in every single aspect of this case has been complete, I cannot say with absolute certainty, but I can say that the majority of it has occurred and that as I said, there is this last aspect of disclosure that is being attended to and in which the Defence are participating. If, however, you require more details about that, then it would seem to me that Ms. Reidy would be the best person to address you on that. If you're concerned about it, I can make arrangements for her to give you a progress report, so to speak, on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We would appreciate that actually. MR. DI FAZIO: You would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Later, yes. Before -- after we finish this witness, for instance. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, I anticipate that the next issue that will arise will be the -- I withdraw that. Okay, after we finish this witness and before the next witness comes along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll see how we progress. We'll see how we go because I'm not happy interrupting Mr. Lazarevic's cross-examination for so long. MR. DI FAZIO: All I would ask is just some indication so that she can marshal her notes and so on and get herself together as far as that is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you're continuing with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: . Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. And good afternoon, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Lazarevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. We will continue where we left off yesterday. This delay you have seen yourself the reason for it, so I will not now go into any explanations. Before we continue with another topic, I would now like to ask two very short questions pertaining to the topic of the white bands. You remember that we discussed it yesterday. Can you please tell me, this obligation to wear such white bands around your sleeves, how long was it in force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not in force for a long time. I may have worn this band for some 7 to 10 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These would be the first 7 to 10 days from the 16th of April or the 17th of April, rather, onwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any cases of people not wearing that band despite the fact that they were of Croat or Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was not the case. Everybody wore such bands, all the people that I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to ask you that as far as you know then. But do you know if anyone, any member of the Croatian or Muslim ethnic group had any -- suffered any consequences because they did not wear such a band, that perhaps they would be arrested or harassed because they didn't wear such a band?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move on to another topic. It is the meeting that took place in late June in the memorial home. You testified about that. You said that Simo Zaric, Mladen Radovic, Jovo Savic, and Vlado Sisic were present at the meeting, that some of them addressed the meeting and that all of them were members of the 4th Detachment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the official date when the Republika Srpska army was established is considered to be the 12th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the 4th of January, 1992, is the day of the Serbian Republic. That was when the assembly split at Pale and when Momcilo Krajisnik split off his faction from the rest of the assembly in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not want to interrupt you during your answer, but I did not mean the time when the assembly was split off. I meant the date when the army of Republika Srpska was established. Do you know that it was the 12th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason why I ask you this is because we have information that in June, the 4th Detachment had already ceased to exist and that at that time it was already the 5th Battalion of the Republika Srpska army. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you some questions regarding Mladen Radovic. Had you known him from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a fellow citizen; you knew where he lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what his function was, in what capacity he was there at this meeting in the memorial hall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that he was the commander of the 5th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that meeting, you and the others who attended the meeting were offered to receive weapons and by that very act to become, as I understand, soldiers of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that means had you accepted this proposal that was presented to you at the meeting, you would have become a soldier of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to move on to another topic and that would be Odzak. In your testimony before the Tribunal, you stated that when you came to Odzak for the first time that the mosque was already destroyed. That's what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the Republika Srpska army entered Odzak, on what date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it be on the 13th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have information that the mosque in Odzak was destroyed on the 17th of July, 1992. Could you confirm this information, the 17th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that I was not there when the mosque was destroyed. I went to Odzak the next day. So I could not tell you when exactly the mosque was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. But in your testimony before the Tribunal, it is in the transcript, page 5087, line 25, you said that you arrived in Odzak for the first time on the 9th or the 10th of July. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we again have a problem with those dates. So according to you, the information that the mosque was destroyed on the 17th of July is not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that it's been 10 years, and I could not pinpoint the exact date. I cannot remember the exact date. I know that it was the beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, if we can look at page 19, line 11, the witness in answering your question, at least according here to the English transcript, says, "I already told you that I was not there when the mosque was destroyed. I went to Odzak the next day." So that presumably would -- if it means a literal meaning what we have -- sorry, a literal meaning of what we have there, whatever the day the witness went to Odzak, he's saying that he must have heard that the mosque was destroyed the day before. So that presumably would give us the date. If you could clarify maybe with the witness that that's what he means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I fully understand what Your Honour means, but in his statement before this Tribunal, the witness stated that the first day he came was 9th or 10th of July, and we have this in transcript. So this is the issue I was really trying to clarify with the witness because there are some misunderstanding obviously. This is why I was insisting on these dates, and again I will ask the witness to start it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So to sum up, you did get the gist of what Judge Williams was saying. So you arrived in Odzak one day after the destruction of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you still maintain that it was the 10th or the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been a really long time, and I cannot tell you specifically the exact date. Maybe it's one day or two days later or earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will not dwell on that any more. Do you know that after the Republika Srpska army entered Odzak that a military administration was introduced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then confirm that the command of the military administration was in the hotel in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the Crisis Staff of the Bosanski Samac municipality had set up a civilian council for Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Savo Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the president of the civilian military council for Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I used to see him in Odzak, but I don't know what his function was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you some questions about certain individuals, just to clear things up as much as we can. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I don't object to -- I'm referring to the question that my learned friend asked, "President of the civilian military council for Odzak." It seems to be a contradiction in terms to me, unless it's some sort of joint body consisting of both civilians and military personnel. If it's the case for Mr. Zaric that there was such a body, then shouldn't it be put to the witness that (a) he can answer clearly; and (b) the Chamber can know what it's supposed to be, this body, because just who was running Odzak might become important in this case. All we know is a civilian military council. What is it, soldiers or the Crisis Staff or is it both or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Right. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm not objecting but I suggest the Chamber would be assisted if that was clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Lazarevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will do my best to satisfy my learned colleague. Civilian military -- what was it -- council was the official name under what this body was formed by the Crisis Staff of Bosanski Samac. I am using its exact name as the way these -- this is the information that I got from my client. Maybe there is another name for this body. Maybe my client really cannot have this information, but I must -- I wanted just to say that it was a body of 15 persons, and my client was one of these 15 persons. I'm not certain about the possibility that this witness could give us a detailed information in regard to this. Maybe we shall wait for Defence case to give all the possible evidence and all the explanation about legal status of this body and everything. So far I'm just interested about persons that this witness possibly saw during that time in Odzak and maybe to clarify with him if he has any knowledge about what were their tasks, what were their position, who was in charge for what. And this is only according to his knowledge. And this is obviously the issue that we're going to deal with, but I don't think this witness is the right one to explain all this. So in this situation, I will just ask him about persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm sure that is clear to Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, it is, and now I know what the position is. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In light of your previous answer, I will not be asking you about some very important functions, posts, tasks, things that you're not aware of. I would just like to ask you some questions pertaining to certain individuals. So I will be mentioning names of people and then you will just tell me that -- whether you know that person or not, whether you used to see him in Odzak or not, and whether you know what he was doing in Odzak or not. So I don't want to ask you any questions as to the things that you are not in a position to know. I will start with Savo Popovic. You already said that you knew who he was. Let me now ask you if you saw him in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding Savo, I said a little while ago that I did used to see him, but I don't know what function he was performing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next person is Cedo Milicevic. Do you know Cedo Milicevic? Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what function he was performing, what he was doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think that he was a minister of tourism.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Odzak for those hotels and so on. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next person is Dusan Gavric. Do you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what post he was at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he replaced Savo Popovic in the function that he was performing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know what that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next person is Milan Ugljesic. The questions are the same. Perhaps you can yourself follow on from there. Do you know him? Did you see him? And do you know what duties he was carrying out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think Milan was a police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miso Pavic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps you're thinking of Mirko Pavic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirko Pavic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the police commander in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ilija Ugljesic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him. I don't know what duties he was carrying out, but he is the brother of Milan Ugljesic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Drago Tadic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rajko Dervenic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mihajlo Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mirko Pavic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We mentioned him awhile ago. He is the -- he was the commander of police in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. We talked about him when I was asking you about the SUP orders. That's the same person who worked at the police in Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Simo Zaric was in charge of security affairs in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you a certain number of questions just now regarding a large number of persons, including my client amongst them, and you answered almost to all of those questions that you don't know what posts these people were at. You don't know the people who were in that council. In your statement before this Chamber on the 4th of December, transcript page 5043 and 50 -- 5093 and 5094, you called a lot of people as -- you called my client a chief.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his question? Could the witness repeat his answer, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the answer of the witness, I think to your previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I will clarify this with the witness again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that he can repeat his answer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the interpreters did not catch your answer, it was a little fast, I will repeat the question again. You described my client as the Supreme Commander in Odzak. We've established that you don't know what duties he was performing in Odzak. Could you please tell me, based on what do you claim that he was the Supreme Commander since you don't know what his function was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that happened in Odzak was first cleared with Mr. Zaric. Everything that was done was done under his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that you said that this both pertained to civilian and military issues; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- I've already asked that, but do you know that the military administration was stationed there? Do you know who made up the military administration, the military component?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that you don't know what my function was in Odzak. I was carrying out my work duty, and I would pass by when Mr. Zaric was directly issuing orders about what to do and where to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you a specific question here pertaining to the military administration and to the question whether there was a military administration you said that you know that there was one and that it was there. Was Simo Zaric in that military administration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the military administration, I used to see him in military uniform, armed, at the hotel with the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think that he was some kind of military administrator of Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to put several questions to you continuing in this same topic. I would like to ask you questions regarding the hotel in Odzak. Simo Zaric's desk was at that hotel. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on the ground floor of the hotel, in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a section screened off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had his desk close to the bar, on the right side as you entered the hotel. As far as any kind of screens, it was -- there was a screen in two sections there at the entrance. It was some kind of panelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I meant. Was the dining-room also in that part of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the workers who were carrying out the work duty in Odzak also eat in that restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a while, very, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood your statement properly, you were sent to go to the work duty in -- to Odzak from Samac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would receive our schedule in Samac, and a group of us would go to Odzak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were told in Samac to go to Odzak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a truck waiting for us in front of the local commune, and then we were taken to Odzak. But we didn't know what we would be doing in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is where you would go onto the truck and then you would arrive at Odzak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We received certain information here that workers who were carrying out the work duty were brought to Odzak, in front of the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later. At the beginning we were brought in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the beginning you were brought in front of the hotel. Later this was changed and after that you were brought in front of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And we would eat, eat our lunch at the SUP afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In Odzak, you and the rest of the workers in Odzak were issued your instructions by Stojan Blagojevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would read a list of persons who were supposed to go to Novi Grad and to those places where we would be working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stojan Blagojevic also check whether those tasks you were given were carried out, whether you had performed your tasks, how far you had performed them? Was that something that he did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, he didn't check up on me. I don't know about others. He did go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've given me a detailed answer regarding yourself and also -- it doesn't matter if you know or don't know about the others. This is sufficient. While you were waiting to receive instructions from Stojan Blagojevic, where we were supposed to go, you said for a while this was in front of the hotel and later it was in front of the SUP. Did you meet in front of the hotel or in front of the SUP, not in those buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the hotel and in front of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know what was happening inside the SUP or the hotel buildings at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were allowed to move freely around Odzak, you had permission to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since this is the kind of work I was doing. I was working on the public water system. I needed to be able to move freely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were able to move freely around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, the interpreter is under pressure. You are not yourself pausing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters and to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We have your last answer. Could you please tell us who issued you this permit to move freely in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given that by the chief of the city water system, Krstan Djordjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like now to move to the topic of the work that you were doing at the farm in Novi Grad. You know about the work about the job that I am talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Again not an objection, but I suggest that the Chamber might be assisted if we knew whether the witness is talking about a permit, a document that allowed him to move around, or whether it was permission, just "You're free to walk around." I don't know but you might find that useful. From looking at the answers, I just can't tell if he's talking about blanket permission, oral permission, or whether he's talking about a piece of paper that enabled him to move around. That might be important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because one may as well ask then, "Why are you saying you are forced to work? You could have left."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will clarify this issue, and thank you to my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, please clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard my learned friend the Prosecutor and also the Judges. Could you please explain to us what kind of a permit or permission it was? Was it a document, a piece of paper which somebody issued to you which enabled you to move freely, or were you just simply told, "You may freely move around Odzak and nobody will stop you."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a piece of paper on which my name was -- my name and last name were printed, and it stated "Permit to move freely around Odzak."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who signed it? Is that the same person that you mentioned? Who signed that permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that this dilemma has now been cleared up about the type of permit. So now we can come back to Novi Grad. Does the name Milan Ugljesic mean anything to you in connection with this topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was a butcher at the farm in Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but was he in charge of this farm or the abattoir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that I used to see him around Odzak but if he was in charge of the farm or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me who told you that you should go to this farm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two police officers brought me in front of the hotel, and I think Dusko Popovic and another person, I think his name was Acimovic, I don't remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is an answer to my question. Can you please tell me who drove you to Samac when you went to get your tools?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: A police vehicle, a police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they used to call him Cigar and I think that was that person Acimovic, Slobodan or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the same person, one of those two people were the ones who actually told you to go to the farm; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that same person brought you back from Samac to Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He brought me to the Odzak hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So he brought you back to the hotel in Odzak. Can you please tell me who took you to Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same two police officers that you mentioned or others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the same ones. We were only -- there was only two of us. There were only two of us, and there was him and his colleague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we will deal with that later. I just want to know whether they were the same people who took you to Novi Grad or were they different people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Novi Grad, who monitored your work there, if anybody did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one soldier. I think he was armed, and he was in a military uniform, and he was a guard at the farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I wanted to ask you about what you've already started to tell me and that is, was anybody else on work duty working at the farm together with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Sead Zigic. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, again I do apologise for interrupting and I'm not objecting, but I want to everyone is following this portion of the evidence. Is my learned friend -- because I have a slight doubt that I am. Is my learned friend -- my learned friend and the witness discussing the episode where he goes to repair pipes in -- at Novi Grad? That's what I understand. I wanted to make sure that the Chamber understood that that was the episode. It's not clearly defined. If you look at the questions, we see a series of questions about work at Novi Grad. It could be just general forced labour. But the witness did describe an episode where I think he alleged that Mr. Simo Zaric participated in giving him instructions to go and repair some facilities at Novi Grad. That's what I understand this is about. But if you read the transcript, it's not immediately apparent. I just wanted to make sure that I've got it right and that the Chamber is -- understands the significance of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have checked very carefully the transcript, and there is only one episode that occurred regarding witness involvement in certain events in Novi Grad and this is the incident where he mentioned the name of my client. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So we are talking about this. Of course I will ask again the witness because I want to make sure that he also understands that we're talking about this very same event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like, since this issue arose, are we now talking about the same incidents or perhaps there are several incidents? Is this the incident in whose respect you mentioned my client Simo Zaric when you went to fix the pipes at the farm in Novi Grad? So this would be the event that we're talking about. So let us now clear this up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I hope my learned colleague is satisfied with this answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we left off when you said Sead Zigic was with you. Was there anyone else from the work duty detail or was it just the two of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you spent a night in Novi Grad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the reception -- at the reception desk, and that is right at the entrance to the farm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me at what time approximately did you finish with your work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 6.00 or 7.00 p.m. At any rate, night fell while we were still there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone check whether you had finished your task? Did anyone control that, verify that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we let the water flow through the pipes, the guard realised that everything was okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after that, you spent the night in Novi Grad and the next day you went back to Odzak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simo Zaric did not tell you personally to go to Novi Grad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not address me. He addressed the two police officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what exactly what I was getting at. So he was not addressing you when he told you to go to Novi Grad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he told one of the police officers that if you failed to do your task --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. We did not get the answer because it overlapped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, the interpreters did not get the answer from the witness to your previous question because there was an overlap between you and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I will again ask this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the same thing happened again. There is an overlap between my questions and your answer. So I will have to repeat my question. So Simo Zaric, when he allegedly said that if you fail to do your task that you should be hanged, he was not talking to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. He was not talking to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to ask you one thing --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I think that time has expired. Maybe we should take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break and continue at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's a question from Judge Singh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: So when he said, "If he fails to repair it, hang him there," who is the "he" that Zaric is referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was talking to the police officers, and he was referring to me, that I should be hanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll continue our proceedings at 1615 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, you're continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I presume, sir, that you remember where we left off after our short break. We were talking about the events, and I asked you if Simo Zaric addressed you and threatened you, saying, "If you don't do this, I will hang you," and then you said that he wasn't talking to you directly, that he was talking to the police officers. If I understood you correctly from what you have said so far, Simo Zaric was allegedly there. There were also the two police officers, you and Sead Zigic. So five persons altogether; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sead was not there. He was at a certain distance away from me. I was standing there with the police officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were the two police officers, yourself, and Sead was a little bit away from you. This fact that you would have been hanged, I presume that you would remember this fact quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a fact that you would have mentioned in your statements.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement dated the 14th and 17th of June, 1996, there is no mention of an event such as this one and of Simo Zaric saying that you were to be hanged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want me to check this with the assistance of the Prosecutors in your statement of that date and then the Prosecution can confirm whether this incident is contained in your statement or not? Would you agree with that procedure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would kindly ask for assistance from my learned colleague from the Prosecution just to check the statement that this witness gave to the investigators of the OTP on 14th and 17th of June, 1996, and to confirm the fact that this episode was not mentioned in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: I'm just attending to that, if I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm just attending to that if I may have a quick look through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, I have a question while Mr. Di Fazio is doing that. And again this might just be the English translation, so maybe you could clarify. Mr. Lazarevic, on page 36, line -- page 36 -- yes, page 36, line 16, in the English, I think you are asking the witness concerning this episode and you used the words, you know, did Mr. Zaric say, "I will hang you," okay? On the other hand, in the responses of the witness earlier on and subsequent thereto, the English is slightly different. He's saying, "The policemen are told you should be hanged." In my knowledge of the English language there is a difference between, "I will hang you," and, "If you don't do this, you should be hanged."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, definitely there is a difference and I will clarify with the witness. For a moment I just lost this page of transcript, and so I -- I haven't noticed that, but I will clarify this with the witness in a very, very -- moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just before you do that, can I also go back to page 5095, when his evidence was first -- the first piece of evidence he gave on this simply said if he refused, hang him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In this line of examination, I will ask the witness about the exact words that he heard that Mr. Zaric allegedly said, and I believe that this is the best way to find as much as we can about this incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you heard this discussion. There are some things in the transcript and also in your previous statement or testimony. Can you please now quote the words, the exact words that Simo Zaric used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: "If he fails to repair it, hang him there."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe this clarifies the situation, so these are the exact words according to the memory of this witness. And I'm still waiting for my learned friend to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio is still looking at the statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: One more question following from that. I mean, did he appear to say that seriously or just to get you to do the work?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard the question that Judge Singh asked. Could you please answer while the Prosecutor is checking the allegations? Did it seem to you that it was said in earnest or that it was said by Simo Zaric in order to make you do your work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It never was clear to me. I know that he did say this, but what the intent was behind these words, whether he was in earnest or whether he was joking ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [no translation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I've checked the statement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MR. DI FAZIO: I apologise. I've checked the statement of the witness and the notes taken by investigators, dated July 1998 and I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it the notes or the statement made by the witness? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I've check both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The counsel was dealing with the statement of the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well. Yes, I've checked the statement, and I can say that in that statement, the statement of the 14th and 17th of June, 1996, in that particular statement, there is no reference to the episode.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Following from that, are those the main -- are those the two main statements that were taken, I mean the substantive statements? MR. DI FAZIO: No. There was one substantive statement, if Your Honour pleases. That was the statement dated the 14th and 17th of June 1996. Thereafter, there was also provided to the Defence another document which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: That's all right. I was just asking if those were the substantive statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If the Defence counsel wants to know what's in the notes, he will raise it. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, throughout the entire period of the war, you yourself experienced some very painful and difficult things, and you know about many other such things that did happen. Can we agree about one thing on the territory -- that on the territory of Bosanski Samac or Odzak, it has never happened that anybody was ever hanged; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move to a different topic, and that is Fadil Mustafic. You know about the episode that we talked about and on which you gave a statement. You've already said that -- that he was your badza, uncle, Simo's wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've already established here that Fadil Topcagic is the brother of Simo's wife, is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Fadil Mustafic is also the uncle of Fadil Topcagic; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So besides the fact that he's very close -- a close relative of Fadil Topcagic, and he's also very close to Simo Zaric through his in-laws, Fadil Topcagic was carrying out the -- Mustafic was carrying out the work duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadil was detained in the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I was asking about the work duty. He was performing that, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a detainee, a prisoner, he did go out to work. First of all in Samac, he was repairing cars because he's a bodyworker, and then after that he was taken to the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, according to my knowledge, he was detained at Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Together with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides the fact that he's closely related to Fadil Topcagic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, you're -- yes, please pause. The pressure on the interpreters --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Again I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So he was detained at Batkovic, despite the fact that he was a close relative to both Fadil Topcagic and to Simo Zaric; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that Dino, Fadil Mustafic's son, paid 4.000 German marks to Fadil Topcagic so that he would bring him out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how do you know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Fadil Mustafic's son Dino.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know it from Dino; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to what you know, did Dino give this in order to pay Fadil Topcagic for a favour or was that supposed to be given to someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Dino gave that to Fadil, according to what Dino said, but I don't know to whom this should have been given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also tell me when this conversation between you and Dino, Fadil Mustafic's son, took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left the camp, I came to Orasje. One time I went to Hungary where Dino happened to be, Fadil's son. He was there in -- as a refugee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this happened in Hungary. If you're able, could you be a little more specific about the period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1995. I don't know whether this was in January or February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to ask you several questions pertaining to the part of your statement relating to the dismantling of the radiators and taking the central heating installation and the radiators to a house in Odzak when Simo Zaric was also mentioned in this context. On that occasion, Simo Zaric did not tell you personally to go and to dismantle the radiators, not to you personally? Did he address you personally and tell you so? You know the question. Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to me. He did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever -- did Simo Zaric ever address you and tell you personally to do anything in Odzak in this context?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He also did not tell you that you should load all that into a truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present when he was telling the driver, not to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer whether this was something that he told you personally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also he didn't tell you where you should take this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, Stojan Blagojevic and Pero Krstanovic were present, according to your statement; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that while you were dismantling the radiators Sead Zigic helped you. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, were any of the workers from the work duty also present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think one of them was the son of Safet Srna, the younger child. I don't know his name. And there was also a man called Dzevad Simnica. That's what we called him. He lived at the railway station in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you took those things which were dismantled, according to your testimony, when you took them to Samac in a truck, was that the same truck that transported the workers back and forth from work duty assignments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, were any of the other workers from the work duty also taken to Samac except yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a couple of them on the truck at that time because it couldn't -- no -- no more people could fit in because there were so much material on the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember names of those two people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Smajlovic Bedrudin, Damir Zurapovic and Zamir Zurapovic. I don't know. I don't remember the names, anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Samac, you unloaded those things out on the street, is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We unloaded it -- them in a courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was in a courtyard. According to your testimony, it was the courtyard of Fadil Topcagic's house. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- was Fadil present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody else other than the people who were unloading these things and yourself, was anybody else present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zigic Sead, myself, the son of Safet Srna, and Simnica and Stojan Blagojevic and Pero Krstanovic, the police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this wasn't delivered to somebody, these things that you unloaded. They were not handed over to somebody, they were just unloaded and left there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to go back to your statement of the 14th and the 17th of June, 1996, and I would also like to ask for the help of my learned friend the Prosecutor so that I wouldn't brother you so that we, with his assistance, can note that this was not mentioned -- this incident was not mentioned in your statement of the 14th and the 17th. So could my learned friend Mr. Di Fazio help me in confirming that this incident is not contained in the statement of the witness of the 14th and the 17th of June, 1996? MR. DI FAZIO: I can't -- if Your Honours please, I can't see it in the statement of the 14th and 16th -- sorry, the 14th and 17th of June, in that particular statement, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After that, you talked with my learned friends from the Prosecution on the 13th of July, 2001. They went to Bosnia at that time, and they talked with you; is that right? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, you mentioned this incident for the first time; is that right?
